As usual, Professor Jack Ponton (Letters, 8 July) cuts through all the smoke and mirrors erected by the renewables industries to give the facts.
He points out the absurdity of the regular and monotonous claims from the wind industry that
sampled:
the intermittent wind turbines cannot provide a reliable power supply. Yet wind is now the largest single power source in Scotland (with a very modest capacity factor), and the main power source for the electricity grid. So a reliable power supply is possible – it's just that the renewables industry is determined to make wind power the only means of providing it.
The renewables industry is, of course, also very keen to present the renewables myth that demand will be higher in 2050 than today. But the renewables myth provides only half the story. The other half is that if we want to avoid the worst climate change, then we need to reduce emissions rapidly. If we do that, then demand will start to diminish. The renewables myth presents a false choice. If we want to avoid climate catastrophe we need to rapidly decarbonise. If we don't, then we can continue to use fossil fuels, as we are doing now, and the renewables myth will not become reality.
John A. Murray
Cull
